events.title: Iran War Escalation
events.summary: The Iran war has escalated, leading to increased geopolitical instability in the Middle East. This has resulted in a surge in oil prices and a decrease in investor confidence. The US has shown military strength, but its waning geopolitical power is a concern.

actions.label: SHORT
actions.target: iShares U.S. Oil & Gas Exploration & Production ETF (IEO)

events.reasoning: The Iran war escalation has led to increased oil prices, which will negatively impact the oil and gas exploration and production sector. On the other hand, gold is often seen as a safe-haven asset during times of geopolitical instability, making it a potential buy.

timeFrame.note: Monitor oil prices and geopolitical developments

events.exitStrategy: Exit when oil prices stabilize or geopolitical tensions ease

events.title: Nvidia Earnings Report
events.summary: Nvidia's earnings report has signaled strong AI momentum, leading to a surge in AI-related stocks. The company's GPU demand has been high, driven by the growing need for AI computing power.
events.reasoning: Nvidia's strong earnings report has made it an attractive buy, while the VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ETF provides a way to rotate into other semiconductor stocks that may benefit from the AI trend.

timeFrame.note: Monitor AI-related news and earnings reports

events.exitStrategy: Exit when AI momentum slows or semiconductor stocks become overvalued

events.title: US Interest Rate Hike
events.summary: The US Federal Reserve is considering an interest rate hike to combat rising inflation. This has led to increased volatility in the bond market and a decrease in investor confidence.
events.reasoning: An interest rate hike will negatively impact long-term Treasury bonds, making them a potential short. On the other hand, a strong US economy and rising interest rates may lead to increased stock market volatility, making the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust a potential buy.

timeFrame.note: Monitor inflation data and Fed announcements

events.exitStrategy: Exit when interest rates stabilize or the economy shows signs of slowing

gains.extendedNote: If the economy continues to grow
